correctness.rationale: The two payoff matrices give a focal payoff difference j-t, with tie retention. Exactly inside a+1..b, an update resamples a random vertex as Bernoulli(p); outside, the count moves monotonically to the corresponding consensus. Reversible binomial conductances establish the displayed winner and Green formulas. Uniform Stirling estimates and Green-kernel sandwich by the i-th term prove the entropy exponents; strict monotonicity of barrier difference proves one crossover. The standalone exact-rational labeled-state verifier passed 33,270 independent Bellman identities in 249 parameter instances. Those tests are finite corroboration, not a substitute for proof.

value.rationale: The finite complete-multiplex game is a natural analytically tractable limit of a published opposing-incentive coordination model. It distinguishes apparent long-lived mixing from true almost-sure eventual consensus, gives the exact finite winner and expected latency, and quantifies a unique natural switch in winning strategy as relative context activity varies. The exponential barrier gives a principled scale for how finite network size masks eventual coordination; this precise quantitative selection effect is motivated by the model, not merely a arbitrary finite cut.
